utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Krajisnik, the Chamber decided that we would allow you some time to add to your testimony, what you considered of importance, and grant you to start with half for that an hour this morning. I do understand that you wanted to provide us with a CD which contains matters which are not translated. This causes, of course again, a problem. I do not know why it is not translated, why it has not been offered earlier to CLSS. Not having looked at the -- what is on the CD, perhaps the best way of doing it would be the following, that whenever you tell us something that, unless it's really necessary to be played or to be shown, that you refer to this material and we'll see whether it can be translated. And if it can, and then of course it's very important that it should be translated within the time granted for cross-examination. So we'll see whether we can give some priority to it. We will also see whether it is not yet -- or whether there is a translation anywhere in this Tribunal so that we could use that translation, and also present it to your down see what they have. So unless you tell us that there's something which we would have to look at now, immediately -- I don't know whether you have any hard copies of what the CD contains. Do you have any?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have copied this CD here in order so that you can have at least this. I also have this DVD, and everything will become clear when I refer to it. Therefore, I would like each participant to be given a copy of this to make it easier to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there's, as such, no harm in that. So at least I'll allow you to distribute the index of ... Yes, I see that there are a lot of folders and some files on it. The folders are -- of course, I can't see what is in the folders. Then, Mr. Krajisnik, I do understand that you have a CD which contains these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- we'll give it temporarily to Mr. Registrar and we'll see what comes us and we'll see to what extent it can be admitted, whether it would be as a contextual document, whether it would be as a document directly introduced by you as a witness. Mr. Krajisnik, please, whenever you refer to any of these documents, please make it clear to us where we find that document on the index of the CD.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I simply make a request? At the earliest, convenient opportunity, might we simply borrow the CD for a few minutes and we can copy it and then we'll have that material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can directly copy --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Whichever, Your Honour; we're happy to do it ourselves or whatever suits the Court best.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course that goes almost without saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We would join in that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That goes much without saying. Whenever there is any chance that this material will be used, you will receive a copy of it immediately. Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I had had a DVD, I would have copied it. I only had one large material, therefore I apologise for not copying it for everybody. Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nowadays copying a CD or a DVD doesn't require much technical skills, even Judges of this Chamber can do it, so ... Mr. Krajisnik, before you start, may I emphasise again that you are speaking as a witness. We leave it to you, that means that you're responding, more or less, to your own questions as an accused. So the witness answers the questions silently put to himself by the accused, which means try to stay out of final argument, try to stay out of argument, and present us, as much as possible, with facts. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The question of he expanded Presidency and work in the Presidency, under 01 there is a document which I wish to tender. This document explains that I was not a member of the Presidency and explains how the consultative body operated. This is a statement made by Radovan Karadzic to our investigators under Rule 92 bis for persons not available, I ask the Court to receive this. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm -- we've been through this in a number of permutations. I'm sure the Court is aware of our position on this. I only add that of course we're entirely unfamiliar with -- of course, first of all it goes without saying that this hasn't complied with appropriate procedures. We've had no chance to either be aware of the interest in advancing this statement in any way. And if there are going to be additional references in Mr. Krajisnik's presentation to statements that were taken by his investigators and that are not and are not likely to be in evidence, I think we should know in advance. I think any reference to those in some manner should be deferred until we have a ruling, as I anticipate it will be, as it has been, that in the absence with appropriate compliance those statements are not in evidence and there's no purpose in referring to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the Prosecution would have wished to cross-examine Mr. Krajisnik if a 92 bis statement -- that you would have insisted on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was this statement taken, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can take a look at the material by your leave. I think it's in 2001 or 2002. I'm only saying it does not meet the conditions of 92 bis, but only the item or the provision referring to people who are unavailable. We have not been able to contact them. I would like to show it, but I will not rely on it. You have taken an oath from me to tell the truth. I am telling you now that there is a statement made by Mr. Karadzic, and I wish to tender it through the regular procedure under Rule 92 bis. And it says exactly who was a member of the Presidency and who wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, for several reasons at this moment the Chamber will not receive that document, one of them being that the Chamber hardly could imagine that it would be anything else than going directly in the direction of acts and conducts of you, as an accused. Furthermore, the whole issue of a presiding officer, the -- which has not been appointed, the problems in calling Mr. Karadzic for cross-examination, so there are many reasons why the Chamber, without at this moment giving a final decision on it because I take it that counsel is better in a situation to assess what argument could still be presented to have it admitted. And therefore, at this moment, the answer is we are not going to look at it, we are not going to give any final decision on admission in evidence, but we just point to you that there are many reasons why we would not be much inclined to admit it into evidence. But we give an opportunity to counsel to argue why it would have to be admitted. They are better aware of the rules and of the case law, and I think it would be not a good idea to leave it just in your hands at this moment to deal with this kind of arguments. At the same time, it is your testimony at this moment, that most likely in 2001 a statement was taken from Mr. Karadzic which -- so therefore exists and might be of a -- well, may have a content which could shed further light on it. So therefore please proceed. We're not going to look at it at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. On the 21st of October, 2001 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's when the statement was taken. I did not intend to tender it. I cannot communicate with my team; that's why I said this. But of course Mr. Stewart and Mr. Jones [as interpreted] will talk to me about ways of tendering it. Your Honours, you asked me to document, if possible, how the discussion was led about Mr. Branko Simic. I sent a letter to the Main Staff on the 26th of October, 1992, about this. I have found those minutes. These are the minutes from the 21st Session of the People's Assembly, and I can provide this document inspection here, if that's the correct way of saying. And I can read a part of those minutes here. I did not have them before because they were not in the documentation. During the cross-examination of Mr. Trbojevic, it was presented by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it is already in evidence. Could the parties assist the Chamber. It's -- so therefore it's an Assembly -- 21st Assembly Session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the document. I can provide it right away, and I can tell you exactly when this was and what item of the agenda it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 21st Assembly Session, would that be the 1st of November? No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's the 30th of October or the 1st of November, 1992, and it's AD 82. Could the usher hand you this document, please? I don't have anymore copies of it. It's at the end of these minutes. Thirdly, I wish to explain briefly Mr. Okun's speech. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's P64A, tab 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will this time be subtracted --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it isn't, Your Honour. That's a mistake --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, not my lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'll find it in a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I only read something from Mr. Owen's book about Mr. Okun and tender it into evidence in connection with his statement concerning the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear no objections, so we have admitted now and then parts of books. Please read it, Mr. Krajisnik. And I take it that you're reading from the B/C/S version but we do know that the book --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and I will tender it in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note they do not have the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 87 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, if you have an English one, could you please put that on the ELMO, if you have it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, while that's happening, we've established that the minutes of this Assembly Session are P583, but the transcript apparently not so far not exhibited. That's what we've been able to track down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, or are you just looking at your screen. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just wanted to be of some assistance. The particular Assembly Session to which Mr. Stewart was referring?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, the 21st Session dated 30th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that we have 30th, 31st, and 1st of November, three dates for the same session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It may have -- sometimes the sessions did last more than a day, Your Honour, but we can double-check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I -- the transcript says November, Your Honour, think I the reference is to October. In any event, with reference to the 21st, the situation is that, to the best of my knowledge, there -- and we addressed this issue earlier when the Court asked for the 1991/1992 Assembly sessions, that with respect to that session there were minutes and at least one brief clip that had been recovered of Dr. Karadzic speaking. And we submitted those. Those, to the best of my knowledge, represent what is in evidence with regard to that session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, limited portion, the remainder could not be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The next session we have just in relation to the November dates is the 22nd Session on the 24th of November, and that has been exhibited in about three places, including P583, but for the moment we don't have any note or suggestion there was sessions in between the 30th or -- 30th and 31st of October. It looks as if it was a two-day session, the 21st Session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second meeting of the steering committee of the ICFY took place on the 20th of October, and in a restricted session Martti Ahtisaari presented a constitutional paper. We have made a direct link between the is situation of hostilities and finding a constitutional settlement. It is being that Warren Zimmerman, the senior representative of the US, stated that it was an impressive document and contained all the relevant principles and wanted to make representations straight away in support of our constitutional idea. We counseled delay, at least until we had presented it to the parties the following day. We said that the co-chairman would be seeking endorsement of these proposals in two days' time in Belgrade and straight afterwards in Zagreb. In the main the steering committee was very sportive and governments' representatives' anxieties focussed on the transitional period. "The Bosnian government was initial enthusiastic to the extent that the foreign minister Haris Silajdzic pulled herb Okun aside and asked that our constitutional proposals be 'imposed' on all parties. In presenting our constitutional proposals to the Bosnian Serbs, we felt the key would be to demonstrate that we had taken the process of decentralisation as far as could without creating states within a state. It's clear here that representatives of the Muslim side attended that meeting and that Mr. Okun and Mr. Zimmerman advocated a change in policy. There are also things that Mr. Zimmerman said here, but since this is not in English, I simply wash to adduce it or have it placed on the ELMO, that this is the policy of neither Europe or America is something I will expound later on through a document I have here. Through plebiscite a question was put here. Mr. Okun said that the territories in the plebiscite where over 50 per cent of the Serbs voted, that he thought this should belong to Republika Srpska or Yugoslavia. The documents I went through here and that I wish to tender into evidence, are very clear. By your leave, I will quote from the minutes from the meeting of the main commission for the implementation of the plebiscite of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina 020831, then the report on the results of the plebiscite which was carried out on the 9th and 10th of November --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Signed by the commission and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, just -- Madam Usher, could you -- 27th of October, which year, Mr. -- you started reading a -- no, could you please leave it but just move it on a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A little bit higher, Madam Usher, no the other way. The text. A lot of reference is to 1995 in the portion prior to that. What year are we talking about when we're talking about the 27th of October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993 when Mr. Okun was a member, with regard to the Vance-Owen Plan. Later on he was not a member; this is well-known. It is not emphasised here, but this is in the book. This is in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now it says that it was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. It may have been -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just a few questions. You say it was presented to all three parties at this moment. The book says that it was in a restricted session of the steering committee. And the next paragraph starts with: "The Bosnian government was initially enthusiastic." And it also say, "We said that the co-chairman would be seeking endorsement of these proposals days' time in Belgrade and straight afterwards in Zagreb. The steering committee at that moment met with all three parties? Is that a correct understanding of your testimony because it does not directly follow from the text of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I just help to this extent, Your Honour. Mr. Krajisnik handed this to the Defence in the bundle of documents last week. Let me hand mine to Your Honour so that at least Your Honour has one in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you -- you say it's 1993 and all three parties were present during this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I made a mistake. It's in 1992, at the very beginning when the Vance-Owen Plan was activated. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we're talking about 1992. And next question was whether all three parties were present during that my colleague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not all three parties were present at that meeting. It was only the Bosnian, or Muslim, side. The plan was presented to us later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now just to better understand -- you said: I simply wish to adduce it or -- that this is the policy of neither Europe or America is something -- you'll expand on that later. So we'll hear about this from you at a later stage. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This plan was not accepted, either by America or Europe later on, and this is evident from the later rejection of the plan. I can briefly expand on what Mr. Zimmermann said about this meeting. He was present there, and that might clarify things. It's from his book, which is also here. It's a short quotation, if you will allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may do so, as long as you keep in mind, Mr. Krajisnik, that this case is not about for what reasons -- at least that's not the core of the case. I wouldn't say that it's totally irrelevant. This case is not about why negotiations, why -- why further talks failed to result in a more peaceful situation. But this case is mainly about responsibility for what happened on the ground. As long as you keep that in mind, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask that the English version be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- could the -- what you read now, is there an English version and could that be put on the ELMO as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I don't have it. You probably have -- it's -- it's Mr. Zimmerman's book.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me help to this extent again. Mr. Krajisnik gave this to us last week. One of the members of our team translated it. The translation is not up to the standard of CLSS, but I'm happy to put it on the ELMO if the Chamber thinks it would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, perhaps that would be a bad idea. Then we'd rather invite Mr. Krajisnik and not present a bad translation -- well, not necessarily a bad translation, a translation which might not be up to standard on the ELMO. Mr. Krajisnik, you're invited to read not too large a portion, and then to read it really slowly so the interpreters can follow you. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just this passage. "Christopher was afraid that the Muslims might reject this plan. I told him I happened to have confidential information about this. A few weeks ago I happened to be in Vance's office in Geneva when Vance and Owen received the response of the Bosnian government to the plan, not only was it positive, it was enthusiastic. The Muslims were ready to support it publicly right away. Vance suggested that they wait. He was afraid that the Serbs might raise the price if the Muslims accepted it quickly." This is in connection with the same event that I've just mentioned. May I say something about Mr. Okun?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said that the plebiscite envisaged a 50 per cent percentage of Serbs in a particular territory. If 50 per cent voted in favour, then it would remain Republika Srpska or part of Yugoslavia, rather. I'd just like to say that there is a report here that in all territories Serbs voted 110 per cent in favour, that is to say that the turn-out exceeded the actual lists. So I'll give you the report from the plebiscite from various municipalities, and I would just like to indicate the following to Your Honours, that that decision that was read out where it says that 50 per cent of the registered citizens of Serb ethnicity, that is paragraph 1, and then there is paragraph 2 and paragraph 3. So I am just going to read what explains the first paragraph. The decisions on the territories of municipalities, local communities, and settlements in Bosnia and Herzegovina that are considered to be territories of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. "Considered," that word means that the people in that area voted in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia. Paragraph 2 as follows: "Parts of territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina from paragraph 1 of this decision, together with the territory of the Republic of Serbia, Montenegro, south Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem," thank you, "constitute the core of the joint state of Yugoslavia." Paragraph 3 reads as follows -- sorry, paragraph 4 rather. "The representatives of the Serb people are hereby authorised, namely Dr. Radovan Karadzic, Professor Nikola Koljevic, Professor Biljana Dr. Plavsic, Momcilo Krajisnik, master of sciences, Professor Dr. Aleksa Buha, Professor Dr. Vojislav Maksimovic, to negotiate with the representatives of the Muslim and Croat peoples about the organisation of future life together in the territory of the hitherto Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." I would just like to add the following. The plebiscite was an expression of the will of the people and that this was not worded very well. Perhaps it's a bit clumsy in terms of what paragraph 1 means, but that meant that negotiations were supposed to continue as to how Bosnia and Herzegovina would be organised. That is 04. Now 05. "Cooperation with The Hague Tribunal." As for that question, there will be no mention of it here, and you will assess whether Momcilo Krajisnik cooperated with The Hague Tribunal. I should just briefly present some facts that are very important. When I was a member of the Presidency from 1996 until 1998, the chief Prosecutor visited me, Ms. Arbour, and I said that I would do my best to make it possible to make all documents available and to have large-scale cooperation with The Hague Tribunal. She asked me whether I would talk to Mr. Karadzic as to whether he would agree to come to The Hague. I talked about that to Mr. Karadzic as well, and he said to me: I have many documents that refute this statement -- or rather, this indictment. And he said that he was prepared to provide all these documents -- sorry, Ms. Arbour before that said if he has documents that refute his statement, we will whole-heartedly embrace this and we are going to make that kind of assessment before a trial would actually begin. I also suggested to Mr. Karadzic that he come to The Hague Tribunal. I have, by way of documentation, this correspondence here that the government provided a great many documents to The Hague Tribunal, everything that they needed, everything that they were supposed to receive. I gave my consent to have all Assembly documents handed over to them, and the last group of documents which includes a letter of the document to the OTP where the government complains that they did not want to receive the last documents that were provided to them by the government. Mr. Karadzic asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue. Mr. Krajisnik, you've told us something about a document containing a number of paragraphs. What's that document, what's the date, and how would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you talking about the question before this question or this document that I am explaining right now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the -- you said paragraph 1 reads, paragraph 2 reads, paragraph 3 reads, and then you explained that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll tell you what document it is. I'll try to be as fast as possible. Obviously I cannot be any faster than this. This is a decision on territories of municipalities, local communities, and settlements in Bosnia-Herzegovina which are considered to be the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, SAO 0214101. You put a question to me last time for me to explain this document, and I did explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, again, just to refresh my recollection. Document issued by whom and at what date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document -- just a moment. A document that was published in the Official Gazette issued by the president of the Assembly -- oh, I'm so sorry. Excuse me, let me just find this. The 21st of November, 1991. Signed by the president of the Assembly, because it was adopted by the Assembly of the Serb People.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you continue by saying: That's 04. I take it that that's a reference to your list? And then you move to 05 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was confused because you went through some paragraphs which came close to four, and then -- so now we have number 5, and number 5 is: "Cooperation with the taking Tribunal." That is a document; which date and given by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0505, and now -- I mean in this survey of yours. And now I am going to tell you exactly what documents these are. It's a letter. The first document is a letter sent by the deputy Prosecutor, Mr. Blewitt dated the 27th of October, 1997; and the second letter, Republika Srpska Ministry of Justice and Administration, 01/2323-S/27, dated the 20th of January, 1997 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do, therefore, understand that under number 5 we find two letters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to cooperation with The Hague Tribunal, at the request of Mr. Karadzic, who agreed to appear before court, he asked for a good lawyer to be provided to him. In agreement with him, I went to Belgrade, because we didn't have any resources, and I wrote a letter which I have attached here. The letter is dated the 17th of March, 1998, where I wrote to Mr. Nikola Sajinovic. And I can read it out here. It's a short letter. It has to do with his lawyer then. Do you allow me to read the letter, it's short, and I would like that to be admitted as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you give priority to that letter, which then seems to deal with the lawyer of Mr. Karadzic, it's your time, Mr. Krajisnik, but I remind you that your time is limited. So please make up your mind whether it has such priority you that you would find it more important than the other documents you still have in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received this document in return from the OTP because it was seized by SFOR. Momcilo Krajisnik, Belgrade, 17th of March, 1998. To Mr. Nikola Sajinovic, Belgrade. "Please provide $2 million USD to us that should be deposited with the Privna Banka Srpska Sarajevo in cash in Pale. These resources would be used exclusively for the legal representation of Dr. Radovan Karadzic in relation to the indictment before the court of arbitration in The Hague. I also hereby undertake to seek your consent for this." I don't know whether this was carried through after my arrest, but this is a document that was presented and that was -- well, I think it would be a good thing if this were to be included in the documentation, if my lawyers agree. After that, Mr. Dragan Hajdukovic was engaged by the OTP in The Hague, and he communicated with our side and he took away a pile of documents, orders, everything that you have here was taken away and handed over to the OTP. I allowed for all these documents to be given to The Hague Tribunal. At one moment when the Office of the Prosecutor refused to receive any further documents, probably considered them to be irrelevant, Mr. Karadzic got angry and said: If they don't want to take these documents, then he gave up on his intention to appear before The Hague Tribunal. I swore before God and before you to tell the truth, but this is this cooperation and I was always prepared to give everything to the OTP, whatever they needed. Many people made statements, then, I made a statement, too. Karadzic was supposed to make a statement as well. Since there were no statements, there was no statement, then I said that it was our investigator who sought this statement. We can tender this document, as I said, if my lawyers agree. And it is on a CD, this document. I'd like to give a number now, this is under 06. On your paper it is under 06. I would like to say that in relation to Mr. Okun you have a document after 31 -- or rather, before -- no, after number 31.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that this was not the policy of the United States of American or -- or of American as such. And could we just look at an excerpt of this book, an excerpt from this book written by Mr. Owen. Could you just place this here? I'm just going to read it briefly. The first part of this part. "The US reaction to our new ideas was more forthcoming than I had expected. President Clinton actually used the word I was trying to avoid - partition - and said they could accept partition as long as it was freely and willingly accepted by the parties themselves." This has to do with the Vance-Owen Plan, and Mr. Owen's visit to President Clinton. There are many documents to show that France and Britain -- sorry, Great Britain refused this plan. The point was actually that this was a plan in relation to the variants that were available that were bandied about. It is true that Mr. Owen and Mr. Stoltenberg did not give up on this -- well, actually a declaration was signed later. So this was a meeting with the former president of America, Clinton. There was this declaration that was signed --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, just for ease of reference if we could have the page number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I'm so sorry. The English page is 192, the Balkan Odyssey. I was reading from the Serbian version, but the page is different. It would be hard for me to find it in English. This position taken by President Clinton was incorporated in a joint declaration - I have it in English and in Serbian - in September 1993. It was signed by Alija Izetbegovic; for Radovan Karadzic it was signed by Momcilo Krajisnik, Thorvald Stoltenberg, and Mr. Owen. I think that this was on the 21st of September, 1993. Paragraph 4, could we place the English text here on the ELMO, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And under what number do we find that in the index to the CD, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After 31, then there is something that's without a number. Joint Serb/Muslim declaration, September 1993. The computer did not accept the number, so I couldn't -- well, see, you have 1, 2, and then the third one is without a number, and then 05-1. Since time is so short, I'm just going to read out the last paragraph. "To this end, it is agreed that the three Bosnian parties will be invited by the co-chairman of the international conference of the former Yugoslavia to meet on Tuesday, the 21st of September" -- oh, I'm so sorry, I made a mistake. I'm so sorry. It's not this page, it's not this passage. Just a moment. Could you please take another paragraph? I made a mistake. It's number 5. "Form a working group for outstanding matters related to the territorial delimitation between the two republics in the envisaged union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, including the areas of Brcko, Bosanska Krajina, the Neretva valley, Eastern Bosnia, and the Ozren mountain, including the natural right of the two republics to access to the sea. This is in addition to the commitment already made to find a permanent solution to the governance of the Sarajevo District within two years. After reaching a mutually acceptable resolution to the territorial delimitation of the three republics within the union and during the initial two-year period of the union's existence, there shall be a provision for a referendum to be held on a mutually agreed date within the republics of the union on the question of whether citizens of any particular republic agree to remain in the union or to leave the union." This has to do with Mr. Okun. Paragraph 19, please. Let me try to -- Your Honours, you saw the Presidency session of Republika Srpska held on the 9th of October, 1992, and it was signed by Momcilo Krajisnik. It was imputed that this was a Presidency session. I assure you that that was not the case. It was not a Presidency session on the 9th of October because in these minutes there is no document -- or rather, this document is on the next page. You see, this is what it says, that at the Presidency session held on the 9th of October, a decision was reached on the appointment of an advisor to the Presidency, Dr. Djokanovic. This clearly indicates that it was a different session and that that was a consultative meeting. Please, if possible, could these documents be admitted into evidence? At that time I was not a member of the Presidency and there is a document -- well, it's an article dated the 9th of October, 1992, and what it says here is exactly what I marked here, that on the 8th of October, 1992, the president of the Assembly of Republika Srpska, Master of sciences Momcilo Krajisnik, and the members of the Presidency of Republika Srpska, Dr. Nikola Koljevic and Dr. Biljana Plavsic, conducted yesterday afternoon exhaustive talks with the commander of the UNPROFOR forces for Bosnia-Herzegovina, Phillip Morillon. Could that be admitted as well so that you see that at that moment Momcilo Krajisnik was not a member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, again I do understand why the reason why you present this is that a newspaper, at least, made a distinction between members of the Presidency and you as a member of the -- you as a -- the speaker of the Assembly or the -- so therefore, I would be inclined to have this translated because it adds, if I may say so, to the -- to the parties --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Some of them suggesting that you were; others, like this newspaper article, that you were not. That's, as such, sufficient. We are interested to see these facts and we do understand that you consider them to support what is your argument, that you were not a member at the time. But that's clear to us already if you say: This newspaper article supports my position, that is that I was not a member of the Presidency, then that's enough for us. Please proceed. And this was under what number -- this newspaper article was under what number in the index?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This article -- well, no. The number is number 10, but this article, I found it late last night, so I am tendering it. It's not on the CD or, rather, the DVD, whereas the other two are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, I invite you to -- to give that document to Mr. Registrar because then perhaps a number for that document, although it's not translated yet, should be assigned. It's clear what it is. It's clear what purpose it serves, and upon being translated we'll finally take a decision on in addition, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that will be Exhibit D238.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're just on this practical matter, I don't know if the CD that Mr. Krajisnik brought this morning is currently being used by anybody for any purpose. If it isn't, Your Honour, if I could borrow it for five minutes I could then copy it and the Prosecution could do the same. I can do that without disrupting anybody. I can do it quietly while the court proceeds, if it's not in use at all. Then we can, with our B/C/S speakers, we can actually make some useful progress on these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want to have it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I will quietly and unobtrusively deal with it and the Prosecution can have it straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, would you give that CD --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, that's very helpful, Your Honour. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're copying it and if it only takes three minutes, could you-- by way of exception make two copies --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I was going to put it on my hard drive, and then I was going to put it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were going to put it on your hard drive. Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 09 and 10, these are two documents. Then -- well, the only thing I can say is that 09 is a series of MUP documents. I have the numbers, too. The OTP has them ordered. 00633311 dated the 24th of October, 1992. The other document is 00633313 dated the 24th of August, 1992. The third one is 00633310, dated the 28th of August, 1992. And -- well, all of these were MUP documents and then this was a press release of the government dated the 17th of August, 1992. The number is 01246820. These are documents which clearly show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are documents which clearly show that at that time the MUP had not been informed about camps or detainees, which is supported by document number 10. It exists in English and in Serbian. The English is in number 0034037 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, at the end of this session, I will not know all these numbers by heart. There's no need of quoting it. The parties now have these documents available. If you want to point to these documents, rather give us the facts contained in those documents rather than the conclusions you draw out of it. If you say this document gives a report of that and that date and you'll find no reference to camps, fine, that's what we understand. To say that a document demonstrates, it's up to the Chamber to see whether it demonstrates this or that, so that's rather argumentative. Tell us that this is a document important because it gives a report but doesn't mention camps, or it expressly denies the existence of camps or whatever, so that we know what to look for on a factual basis rather than on what kind of conclusions you draw out of it. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I think the Court said this but by urging Mr. Krajisnik not to recite ERN numbers, I wanted to underscore the need to identify the document by a date or some other identifiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say it's a MUP document, by that and that date, we know better than giving all these numbers, so if you could keep all of this in your mind when you proceed which you are allowed to do now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 10 is a letter from Mrs. Plavsic dated the 10th of September, 1992 -- excuse me, the 9th of September, 1992, in which she confirms that she doesn't know about the camps, she doesn't know about rapes, and so on, which shows that the Presidency and the leadership did not know about these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Krajisnik, what it shows we'll find out. It's a letter in which -- yes -- in which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's apparent that she doesn't know that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The letter of the 17th of August, 1992, by Minister Stanisic. I can only say that it's not on the CD, and he says here that he is not aware that there are camps and he's not aware of any conditions in camps. This document has an ERN number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps this is a document, since it's not on the CD, which needs a number. If you would please give it to Mr. Registrar, I take it, Mr. Registrar, it would be D239?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be a letter from Mr. Stanisic addressed to whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To all the security centres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's D239, it still has to be translated. So no decision yet on admission. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 001082, these are two documents used here. One is a Tanjug report, the other a BBC report, the former in Serbian, the latter in English, transmitting a statement by Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we find them on the CD?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 08-1 and 08-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose of this is to show who was a member of the Presidency and who was the president of the Assembly. 0702. The main point is that parallel institutions were created by the Serb side on their own initiative, and I said that on the 30th of March, 1992, Mr. Izetbegovic made a statement in connection with the declaration. I can read it out and I wish to have the part I have marked translated in order to show that this happened before the regionalisation. If I may read it, I will be brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. Krajisnik, I've just consulted my colleagues on what we are doing at this moment. What you are doing at this moment is trying to get introduced as -- well, a lot of documents you find of importance. Nevertheless, to do this all in court and to say this is a document what says this and this is a document what says that, of course we could read that and they are -- the way they are handled at this moment make them almost contextual documents rather than anything else. The suggestion would be - and I'm also looking at both Prosecution and Defence to comment if they would disagree with such solution - is that you select the documents you consider of major importance, that you add to each document not more than three lines saying: This document is for this and this and this reason important, and then have this material translated as quickly as possible, and then to see whether we can -- whether we can accept them as contextual documents. We'll hear from the Prosecution whether it's a known document to them, whether they oppose, admission, or -- because at this moment you read one -- couple of lines from a document, we don't know the remainder of it, we don't know -- very often it's -- takes us some time to find out what date it is, who wrote it, which doesn't add -- would not add very much to what I suggest. Mr. Josse, Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, that -- that's not problem for the Defence and seems a very practical solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and it's not -- it's not a promise to admit these documents, but it's a suggestion for a more efficient way of handling these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just mention while I'm on my feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's taking slightly longer than five minutes because the volume on the CD can't copy over in that time, but once it's done I'll hand it over to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the -- how many megabytes or gigabytes, is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, at the moment, Your Honour, it's -- I didn't check that first. It tells me I've got another 11 minutes fro it to copy over. It's actually quite a bit, Your Honour, and as soon as soon as I've finished copying Honour. Once I've done I'll hand it over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see most of the documents are .pif and .tif documents and hardly any word documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I wanted to explain why it's taking longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Krajisnik, if it's too much I want to say that the material varies in, at least, relevance as far as we can see at this moment of course, which is not a final judgement on the relevance but it seems to be varying. But, Mr. Tieger, I first give you an opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. For the most part the Prosecution has no objection to the Court's pragmatic suggestion and solution. Our one concern is that the description or the additions to be provided by Mr. Krajisnik may take on a testimonial aspect. And if that's the case, we would want to -- we would urge the submission of that material, obviously, as quickly as possible so that if they need to be cross-examined they can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps the first thing we should have translated is then the three lines explanation of what the document is because that might give you a clue already on whether there's any testimonial aspect or whether it's really just describing the document. Mr. Krajisnik, you are invited to present the document and we'll later decide what size we would even consider -- you'll also invited to put them in order of priority so that if we say it's too much, it's too late, then at least we start striking them from the bottom and not from the top. So it's your responsibility, every document you're allowed three lines to explain what this document is. Please keep in mind -- and of course in your description of the document, of course you -- it may be clear to us if, for example, you say: This is a newspaper article which -- which characterises my position as a president of the Assembly, then it's clear to us that the importance for you would be that it does not characterise you as a member of the Presidency because we all know that it's undisputed that you were a member of -- that you were the president of the Assembly or speaker of the Assembly. So please, priority. Describe them, but as factual as possible. Three lines each document, and those descriptions will be the first ones to be translated which might guide us, as well, in allowing further -- in allowing further translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 3.53 gigaytes which actually -- I've been referring to it as a CD, it's obviously a DVD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, must be a DVD. Mr. Krajisnik, you're invited to present these comments within the next two days because it comes at a very late stage. The three lines comments or description of the documents is immediately needed by the Prosecution to further orient itself on the matter. So you're invited to do that within two days. Yes. Then -- yes. There's -- apart from all the documents, there's one other matter which I would like to raise already and that is the statement of Dr. Karadzic. I mean, perhaps I was a bit quick in saying that it might go to the acts and conducts of the accused. Of course that's not said yet. Of course we do not know anything about it. In order to make it at all possible on which might be an important document for Mr. Krajisnik, it seems at least that he finds it important. It might be just as important for the Prosecution. And of course it's -- I take it also that it's -- depends on the content of whether cross-examination would be desired. But we can't say anything about that unless at least there is a translation. So I would at least give a start with a translation of any statement of at least a person who was close to Mr. Krajisnik at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I only rose to ensure that the provisions of 92 bis weren't hurdled past until the document was reviewed and the efforts the Court referred to were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've got an English translation of this statement and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, if you would be able to provide it to the Prosecution so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And even unto the Chamber, Mr. Krajisnik wants it to be a present to everyone admitted into evidence, and then we would have to look at the -- apart from the formality -- well, we have to look at the formalities. We have to look to whether the content goes to the acts and the conducts of the accused. So therefore, to make any discussion about it not without factual basis, please provide it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We'll do that, Your Honour, there's no point in creating extra work. We only take the point about the 92 bis procedures. Karadzic is currently not available for cross-examination, which is one of the items mentioned in Rule 92 bis or at least that's how we last heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we heard as well, and therefore it might be of importance to know based on the content whether the Prosecution would -- would insist on calling Dr. Karadzic under those circumstances for cross-examination. If they would and he's not available, then of course an admission problem would be there, not to say what the outcome of that problem would be. So, Mr. Krajisnik, are the instructions clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am deeply grateful. I will explain this very briefly, but let me just ask, Mr. President. I had intended to tender a few more documents which I did not have time to prepare last night before last. I was up all night working. Could I explain those as well, they are important documents? And secondly, I am not able to communicate with my counsel and I certainly wish them to take an active part and evaluate this. I simply prepared this, but I was unable to speak to them because I am not allowed to communicate with them. So it was not something that I decided on my own; I just wanted to ask them to tender this into evidence, this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, at this moment you were given an opportunity to add whatever you thought, as a witness, whatever you thought important to add to what has been said during your testimony. If you consider these documents important, please tell us what they are -- I mean, there has been so much time to prepare for your examination that -- and you may have spent so much time on it that you just follow at this moment what you, as an intelligent man, considered to be important to add. And if this includes documents, please give them to Mr. Registrar if they are not on the CD, and a number will be assigned. And tell us clearly what's the date of the document, what it is, from whom it comes, to whom it was sent, and then again in one or two lines saying it explains the position of Mr. X or Mr. Y as a deputy of Bosanski Novi, whatever it is, but just a brief description, and of course any comment at this moment, if you would like to add.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly Mr. President, to give a brief explanation because I have based everything I have to say additionally on these documents. I have nothing else to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you just want to say: Please look at this document because it's important for me, then just describe it. If you like to say: Here we have a document which clearly contradicts the testimony of Mr. So -- or at least should be considered in relation to the testimony of Mr. X, Y, or Z, or where he said that the barracks were left on the 30th of April, but this document, as you can see, says it was on the 25th of April, then we know what it is about, why you present it. So please do that as efficiently and as concisely as possible. Perhaps -- let me just ... [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, how many of these documents are there that you wanted -- so that are not on the CD?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, three or four perhaps, five at the most. I found them late last night. It's not a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Prepare it well during the next break. Five documents, three minutes each, which would allow you another 15 minutes after the break. We'll -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there's one matter. The Defence is wondering when we might receive Your Honour's decision on the certification application because it's clear that the -- with respect, the time has come when that is needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I will let you know this morning when you could expect that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Matters stand as they are. If we give a certification, that would mean that we'll just proceed until the Appeals Chamber has given its decision on it. If we do not give the certification, the same would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the Defence does not, with respect, accept the first of the two propositions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do not see -- is there any authority at this moment which you say if we appeal a decision that would stay the effect of the decision as it has been given? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, our position is that it gives rise to -- in one of the two alternative situations, it certainly does give rise to the question of a stay. We would like, Your Honour, to know where we are on that application, which was made several days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, we note Your Honours didn't invite, and the Prosecution have not indicated that they were responding in any way, so we assume that that -- that particular issue whether the Prosecution respond went by the board days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it if the Prosecution would have wished to respond, they would have indicated so, although time has not elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's what we assumed, Your Honour. Maybe they mentioned it to me or Mr. Josse and I forgot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll look at it. We'll also look at whether we can come up with a decision quickly and then have it in writing to be delivered at a later stage, whether we would announce to you when the decision will be delivered in writing, whether there's any reason to stay. I'm just now working on the -- from the top of my head, but I don't remember that there was a request for a stay --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we haven't had Your Honour's decision yet, and we have not made any submissions on that. Your Honour, we're trying to take things in the proper, logical sequence. Your Honour, the application for a stay doesn't arise unless Your Honour's decision is in a particular direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But that is the position, Your Honour, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Of course you could anticipate on to say if the Chamber would not be inclined to give such a decision for these and these reasons, we would like to have your present decision stayed. There's nothing illogical in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: There's nothing illogical, Your Honour. There's enough real stuff to deal with, without a hypothetical as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll report to you after the break what you could expect from us at this moment. We'll stand adjourned until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can announce that the request for certification -- that the decision of the Chamber is that it is denied, but it will be put down on paper in a written decision. And you will receive that somewhere in the coming days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's most helpful to know that now. We appreciate that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, for five documents, three minutes each. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first document is a decision on the return of displaced persons in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It should be placed on the overhead projector. It would be very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Date of the decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision that was signed by Mr. Karadzic on the 2nd of June, 1992. And it was here on the agenda. What I wish to indicate is the following. The date of the 20th of May was in dispute, and in the heading it says that it was reached by -- let me read this out. "On the basis of article 81, paragraph 2, of the constitution of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the acting presidents of the republic are reaching the following decision," and that's Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Koljevic who were in that position until the 12th of May. That was just my objective, to provide this explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Registrar -- Madam Registrar, I have to change during the day. Gender issues in the UN are very sensitive. That would be D240.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No decision yet on admission since there's no translation yet, or is there? But the parties are invited to see whether it's in evidence already, so this is a provisional assignment of the number. Next one, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to provide two or three pages, that is 130, 131, up to -- oh, I beg your pardon. Just a moment, please. Up to 137 of this book written by academician Muhamed Filipovic, I was Alija's Diplomat. The referendum is explained here -- or rather, the Assembly that discussed the referendum on the 20th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is a document stemming -- although from later but by someone who was involved in these events and to read what he wrote about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He was a member of parliament.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, that would be number D241, I take it? Yes. Thank you. Same is valid in relation to the other documents since there is no translation yet. No decision is taken on admission, it's just provisionally assigning a number. Next document, Mr. Krajisnik. I already can see that it's a document of the 9th of May, 1993, if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: June I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, June, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, 1993. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is an order issued by Mr. Karadzic to make it possible for civilians and soldiers of the HVO to pass through, that is to say Croats. Who fled to Serb-held territory due to a Muslim offensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps one would --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how this document can be treated, perhaps as a contextual one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One line on what -- of course I see that you tell us that Mr. Karadzic made it possible for civilians and soldiers of the HVO to pass through. Is this to underline the proper humanitarian approach taken by Mr. Karadzic at that time? Is that how we have to understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to say that there was no plan of genocide against the Croats. That is the core of the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. By letting them out you would say that would contradict any genocidal plans. Yes, that's clear. That would be D242. Yes. The next document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the 1st Krajina Corps dated the 23rd of June, 1992, in which it says that an order was received from the Main Staff that every soldier should be familiarised with the application of humanitarian law and observance of the Geneva Conventions. I just have to provide an attachment here as well, that is to say who this was sent to, that is to say all units of the 1st Krajina Corps. And then up here it says: "On the basis of the positions of the Main Staff of the Army of Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina with a view to guiding the members of the 1st Krajina Corps that we continue to wage the war in a soldierly and honourable way. I hereby issue the following order," and then it goes on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be D243. And you say there is an attachment to it, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Please, please, I'll provide it now as soon as I finish this. Could you just wait a moment, please, and then I'll give you this attachment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, Madam Registrar, did you receive D240, 41, and 42, the originals that were presented by Mr. Krajisnik? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could I give this attachment later? I don't seem to be able to find my way. Perhaps I could do it during the break. It's just a list of the persons that it was submitted to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So D243, the order for the Main Staff and attachment of addressees --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, I've just found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it clear -- can we have it on the ELMO for one second?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please a bit up, Madam, the upper part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is an OTP number at the end as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I just have D243 together with this attachment, could I just have the two of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a draft agreement on the tripartite exchange of territories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I draw the attention of the parties, although the document doesn't say anything about a relation between the order itself and the list of addressees, that I see that the printing information makes this one, the first one, KP22010L, and the list of addressees, KP22010M, which suggests a sequential order. And the same is true for the ERN numbers, the order ending 860, the list of addressees ending 861, which is a first indication that what Mr. Krajisnik said, that this list belongs to his order might be true. Madam Registrar, would you please keep them together. The two documents together are D243.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next document, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a general framework agreement on the trip or tight exchange of territories and demilitarisation of state borders. This is based on an agreement reached on access of Republika Srpska to the sea made in Dayton in 1995, that is what is said down here. This is just a contextual document that this access to the sea was being discussed all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be D --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be D244.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are three documents about the visit of the president of France, Mr. Mitterand. There is something very important here. The newspapers are Glas, dated the 29th of June, and here it says he paid in visit on the 28th of June, he paid this visit to Sarajevo when the agreement was reached on the handover of the airport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom out just a tiny little bit. Zoom out, please. Yes. I see it's Glas, 29th of June, 1992. Is that -- I have difficulties in reading it, but -- yes, Glas, 29th of June, 1992. Yes. And please continue, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within this -- actually, just this small excerpt where President Mitterand says on the 3rd of August that rumours should be looked into as to whether there are any camps in Yugoslavia. So on the 5th of August he gave instructions to that effect because the Serb side was saying one thing and the others were saying something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please have a look at the head of this page to see about the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The date can be seen right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see Paris, the 5th -- could we zoom in on the article? Yes, it reads: "Paris, the 5th of August."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the headline says: "Searching for the truth."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes, what as a matter of fact the -- the fact that President Mitterand insisting on the matter having to be investigated, what that adds to what we know already is unclear to me, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He paid a visit to -- he paid a visit to Sarajevo, and he heard contradictory claims made by the two sides that actually deny --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, do we not have already a huge amount of evidence on which the parties disagreed on whether any camps existed, yes or no? I mean, we have so much evidence, the one saying there were not, the other saying there were. International news media --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Okun said that the Serb side admitted that there was ethnic cleansing and that there was camps. I'm just saying that there were different opinions involved. I am saying here that he heard different views and that he is seeking the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This seems to be the 16th of August, also from Paris, and it is also a publication in Glas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. This statement has to do with Mr. Kouchner. The headline is: "There are no concentration camps in Bosnia." And I can tell you why I think this is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just read such headlines and I made inferences on the basis of that. I don't know whether this is correct, but I'm just telling you the way it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your testimony then is that you oriented yourself on statements given by foreign politicians on whether or not there were camps? Then I have misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I was just trying to explain that I did not have any information whatsoever except for our people who were telling me that that was not correct. I did not have -- I did not have any other information that was stating that this was correct. My objective is for me to say that in our media there was nothing that would indicate that camps existed. So in addition to the information received from Karadzic, Koljevic, and Plavsic, I only read that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That's -- Madam Registrar, that would be three press clippings, and could you please -- if it could be given to me. What I will do is I'll -- with a blue pen, I'll indicate what portions -- yes. The second clipping doesn't say from which newspaper it comes, but at least it has a date and it's a publication in relation to what was said by Mitterand on the 5th of August. The three clippings together, Madam Registrar, would be D245?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And only the portions I indicated need translation. Mr. Krajisnik, you said five documents. We are now at six, one of them a bundle. Any else -- any other document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, I have two more documents. May I present them -- I mean in addition to the one that's on the ELMO now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then try to do it in four minutes. On the ELMO we have now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a document dated the 7th of August, 1992. It seems to be a letter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Written by Mr. Karadzic and addressed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the Prime Minister, Mr. Djeric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what's the importance of this letter for us to see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is important is that he is informing him about Mr. Samaruga's report and he's issuing a letter to him to the effect that his institutions should take all measures related to prisons. So this was between the Prime Minister and the President of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Resulting from the Samaruga report. Next one would be, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D246. Next one, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If these maps have not been admitted, could they please be admitted now, the proposals of the parties before the Cutileiro plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We see two maps published in a newspaper article it seems. Which one could -- could I just have a look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three maps, three maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have Politika the 19th of March, 1992. I see at this moment two maps. Where is the third one? There is the third one. Three maps proposed by the parties in the context of the Cutileiro negotiations. Is that what we should look at, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think that we have such maps in evidence at this moment. This was published apparently; that would be D247. We come to the last document, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, what is it? It is a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a report from a session of Prosvjeta in Brcko that the first OTP witness, Mr. Gasi mentioned. There's a report here stating that Momcilo Krajisnik was not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does it explicitly say that you were not present or is it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Here it says who was present, and it certainly would have been registered, had the president of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina attended, because this is a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have two totally different documents. We saw a first page which is taken from what -- could we first go back to the first page? This is published where? Where is it taken from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was published in the newspapers, and the other part -- I mean, that's the 18th of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One by one. Do we know what newspaper it was published in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say now, but the date is written here, the 18th of May, 1991, underneath this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there is another date at the bottom of the -- could we just zoom out as a whole and go to the bottom of the -- yes. Could we zoom in on the very bottom of this publication. It says also the 18th of May, 1991. Okay. So this was published in an unknown newspaper. Next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the speech made. [Trial Chamber, Legal Officer, and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krajisnik, we were at the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the speech made by the representative of the Croatian society called Napredak at that same celebration. And also the speech made by the representative of the Muslim cultural society, Preporud. And on the first page we saw the speech of the Prosvjeta, the Serb society.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the first page we saw a newspaper clipping, which is of course a bit different from the text like on the other two pages. What's the origin of the other two pages? Was this provided by those who have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
